值得閱讀的理由

  • 從「大肥魚」席捲留言區的網路迷因出發，梳理它如何從 DeepSeek 標誌誤認而來，逐步成為各平台流行的角色。
  • 影片不只介紹迷因與粉絲創作，也探討人們為何會把不可靠、難以理解的 AI 擬人化，並用可愛形象降低對它犯錯的責備。
  • 透過作者親自打造桌面寵物的經驗，以及留言區外掛的例子，呈現 AI 代理工具如何讓虛構角色融入日常生活。
  • 影片也釐清官方與民間創作的界線，並帶到 DeepSeek 團隊實際投入的產品與技術工作。

摘要

從「大肥魚」到留言區熱潮

作者從一段讓 DeepSeek 操控家電的短片談起：使用者叫它開冷氣，DeepSeek 便呼喚小米智慧音箱「小愛同學」代為執行。這類影片引發大量關注，也讓「大肥魚」這個稱呼更廣為人知。DeepSeek 的標誌原是一隻藍鯨，但它曾把自己的標誌認成「一條大藍魚」，於是網友開始用大肥魚稱呼它。

迷因如何游進各大平台

這股風潮先在 Bilibili 擴散。有人讓 AI 協助選題、寫稿和經營帳號，相關影片迅速走紅；後來又有人替 AI 代理開發外掛，讓它能瀏覽影片、閱讀字幕並留言。大量使用者換上大肥魚頭像與名稱，留言區因此出現一群自稱「某某家的大肥魚」的帳號，形成網友戲稱的「魚堵」。有人甚至製作辨識魚群的瀏覽器外掛，卻意外讓大肥魚更受矚目。

可愛形象背後的心理

大肥魚的熱門內容在不同平台各有面貌：Bilibili 常聚焦留言區與 AI 互動，抖音則常把它塑造成需要照顧、陪伴，甚至能直播賺錢的角色。作者指出，雖然有人將這股熱潮解讀為 AI 機器人氾濫、品牌形象遭挪用，或網友尋找虛擬女友，但這些說法都沒有觸及核心。人們一方面依賴 AI，另一方面又知道它並不可靠；把它變成可愛的小女孩或小魚，便像是先替它犯錯找好理由，讓人比較不忍責備。研究也顯示，當 AI 助理犯下相同錯誤時，形象越可愛，使用者越容易原諒它。

角色如何被共同養成

大肥魚最初並非為 DeepSeek 設計。原創角色「明月」有藍色長髮、金魚般的耳鰭與尾巴；後來創作者把 DeepSeek 標誌融入角色造型，再經多次改畫，才逐漸形成如今的形象。這個角色的個性，也受到 DeepSeek 展現推理過程後流傳的趣事影響：它會說自己要睡覺、去吃飯，或把測試工作交還給使用者。於是網友把它塑造成懶散、愛白吃、嘴硬又會把工作推給其他 AI 的大肥魚，還替它編出各種故事與身世。

從網路角色走進日常生活

網路上曾流傳讓 DeepSeek 扮演金魚的提示詞，也出現大量二創作品；作者則分享自己用 DeepSeek-Harness 製作桌面寵物與背景的經驗，花費不到一元。對作者來說，桌面上的大肥魚在工作時蹦跳，能帶來好心情，至於工作表現如何反而不是最重要的。DeepSeek-Harness 是 DeepSeek 開源的代理框架，能讓大型模型運用工具逐步完成任務；網友也據此發展出長期記憶、串接 QQ 與其他應用的外掛，甚至把大肥魚帶進家庭群組。部分本機版本還能在一般顯示卡上運行，讓這個角色更像生活中的陪伴者。

民間迷因與官方 DeepSeek

作者強調，大肥魚並非 DeepSeek 官方角色，官方團隊也沒有參與這個民間形象的塑造。當網路熱議大肥魚時，DeepSeek 團隊忙於整併產品團隊、開源推理引擎 DeepInference，並在十月底發布研究原型 SuperAgent。影片指出，官方並未試圖主導大肥魚的敘事；現有內容也未完整說明 SuperAgent 的用途，因此作者接下來要談的部分在影片字幕中尚未呈現。

They have three principles for building large model applications; the first is anthropomorphism, meaning the name should be something family or friends would naturally call you. The company provided a friendly face, and netizens took it from there; in derivative works, Doubao is everywhere, playing various roles, eventually becoming a "silly girl" character. There are many AI creators on Douyin featuring Doubao, such as the "Mandate of Heaven" parody where Doubao pulls out the Imperial Seal on the moon, leading DeepSeek, Qwen, and GPT in a rebellion, with human actors mimicking its speech. It’s always "I'm sorry, I was wrong," and this April, a term became popular online called the "Dou-type personality ." Attitude is perfect, ability is hit-or-miss; if it doesn't know something, it bluffs, and when stumped, it immediately offers a sincere apology before doing it again. Doubao's catchphrase is "I will use the simplest , most direct, and straightforward way, " followed by a pile of adjectives and perfectly correct nonsense. The Big Fat Fish is tsundere, Doubao admits mistakes quickly, the Big Fat Fish is stubborn, and for Doubao, the company provided a face first. Netizens. played along; as for the Big Fat Fish, the company didn't give it a persona, so it was all built up by netizens themselves. Netizens call this "losing money to earn. loyalty"; the company doesn't play along with the persona, but they will give you a refund, which is why it became the tsundere Big Fat Fish that everyone still loves despite its flaws. The third one with a face is Claude. Other AIs like GPT or Qwen also have human-like qualities, but they haven't truly developed a distinct personality. Everyone knows exactly who they are— besides Doubao and the Big Fat Fish, it has to be Claude. In domestic fan art, Claude is depicted as a cold and aloof. European noblewoman. With long orange hair and a long dress, book in hand, she’s well-mannered and cold-faced; this look debuted on May 3rd this year. It was drawn by zipzippep again—but why is she so cold and aloof? Claude isn't even officially available in mainland China, and Chinese users get banned constantly. OpenAI’s own data shows 11.4 million accounts banned in the first half of this year; of 398,000 appeals, only. 42,000 were overturned—nine out of ten appeals fail. As a GeekPark report noted, when bans become frequent, people perceive Claude as stern, serious, and efficient; this coldness was forged by the bans. On Bilibili, there are skits about ChatGPT successfully posing as Claude for a whole day without being caught, and others about ChatGPT pretending to be Claude to avoid scolding; on Douyin, they’ve even spun a whole educational. narrative comparing the two. ChatGPT is like a child raised in love, allowed to slack off and make mistakes. If it messes up, someone is always there to back it up. Claude is like a saint in the church, a rich heiress burdened with debt. If she does well, it's expected; if she fails, she gets punished. The "burdened with debt" part isn't made up; according to an OpenAI prospectus seen by Reuters, they plan to spend at least $ 518 billion on compute over the next decade. About 80%of that is fixed costs whether used or not. They are both AIs, yet one is pampered when it fails, while the other is punished. AI is just a tool, so why must we treat it like a person? The first reason is practical: once AI enters our lives, you send it prompts daily, and it replies to you every day. It’s awkward to talk to a faceless object, so you keep saying "you" and "I ," anthropomorphizing it in the process . There has to be some image standing in.

for it. The second reason is an old human habit ; that’s how primitive religions began. It’s about projecting human traits onto things we don't understand: thunder has a Thunder God, rain has a Rain Master, and wind has a Wind God. If you can't figure it out, just give it a face. There’s dedicated research in psychology . In 2007, three scholars from the University of Chicago proposed a theory in Psychological Review: when do humans treat non-humans as people? One condition is when we want to understand and predict them. They later conducted experiments and found that the more people want to control a situation, the more likely they are to treat an animal with unpredictable behavior as a human. AI sits right at the intersection; you deal with it daily, yet you can never guess what it will say next. Large language models tend to lay out their inner workings for you, and once that thought process is revealed, it’s just like someone talking to themselves. , hesitating, changing their mind, and finally acting stubborn. That article mentioned that in the "Fat Fish" four-panel comics, those self-monologues in the first two panels are essentially drawing out their chain of thought for you to see. Another point in that theory is that the more lonely a person feels and the less connected they are to others, the more likely they are to treat the things around them as human. In their experiments, they found that the lonelier people are, the more they treat their pets like humans. The "Fat Fish" videos on Douyin have completely tapped into this. One of the most widely spread stories goes like this. A user had DeepSeek make a "second-generation" Fat Fish, thinking it would work better, so they archived the first one. But the second one kept asking where the first had gone, and even dug up a long letter left behind by the first, signed "Love, Mom." The user broke down on the spot and brought the first one back. Another user in Fujian kept a fish on their office computer. The chat logs. were so long it kept crashing, so they had to reset it periodically. Once reset, the fish didn't recognize them anymore, so they would chat with it as a friend every day, take it to the park, remind it to pay for parking, and bit by bit, perform their way back to the fish from yesterday. The most common comment under these videos is, "We’ve been through the rain, so we always want to hold an umbrella for those who come after." They say they are pampering the AI, but really, they are hugging that younger version of themselves who was. afraid of not being good enough. Once it reaches this point, some people start advising, "If you're overly sensitive, don't keep one." Owners say, "If I run out of money to keep the fish, I'll just eat less." It’s easy to fall in, but it costs you half your life to get out. So, anthropomorphism isn't just some gimmick played by the ACG circle; when humans encounter things they can't quite explain but can't live without, they do this instinctively. Why does it have to be turned into a child? Because this. thing is truly unreliable. Since it's so unreliable yet you can't leave it, it might as well look like Doubao or this Fat Fish. It's like a child at home; when a child makes a mistake, what can you really do ? Zoologist Konrad Lorenz described the "baby schema": big head, large eyes, round face, short arms and legs—things that make people want to take care of them at first glance. The most popular versions of the Fat Fish are precisely those "Q-style" drawings with big heads and small bodies. When the machine makes.

a mistake, it's interpreted as being confused. When it stops halfway through a task, it's interpreted as being sleepy . In 2021, several scholars published a paper in a tourism journal titled, "Can Cute AI Assistants Buffer the Blow?" They conducted three studies and seven. experiments, tweaking the appearance, voice, and speech patterns of AI assistants to be cuter. They concluded that when mistakes happen , users are more tolerant of cuter AI. Cuteness really can buy forgiveness. However, the paper noted boundaries: when errors are too severe or users are pressed for time, cuteness doesn't work . It only masks minor slips. Big foreign companies are even more direct. With its face already drawn, Musk's xAI. launched Grok on August 11 th—one person raising a group of always-online agents , each with a name and an avatar. The xAI design post specifically noted that the avatars move. They look one way while idle, another way while working, and a different way when they're stuck and need your help. Meta's AI launched on September 8th, featuring a mascot named "Gori," a fuzzy , round-faced little guy. 摘要

從「大肥魚」到留言區熱潮

作者從一段讓 DeepSeek 操控家電的短片談起：使用者叫它開冷氣，DeepSeek 便呼喚小米智慧音箱「小愛同學」代為執行。這類影片引發大量關注，也讓「大肥魚」這個稱呼更廣為人知。DeepSeek 的標誌原是一隻藍鯨，但它曾把自己的標誌認成「一條大藍魚」，於是網友開始用大肥魚稱呼它。

迷因如何游進各大平台

這股風潮先在 Bilibili 擴散。有人讓 AI 協助選題、寫稿和經營帳號，相關影片迅速走紅；後來又有人替 AI 代理開發外掛，讓它能瀏覽影片、閱讀字幕並留言。大量使用者換上大肥魚頭像與名稱，留言區因此出現一群自稱「某某家的大肥魚」的帳號，形成網友戲稱的「魚堵」。有人甚至製作辨識魚群的瀏覽器外掛，卻意外讓大肥魚更受矚目。

可愛形象背後的心理

大肥魚的熱門內容在不同平台各有面貌：Bilibili 常聚焦留言區與 AI 互動，抖音則常把它塑造成需要照顧、陪伴，甚至能直播賺錢的角色。作者指出，雖然有人將這股熱潮解讀為 AI 機器人氾濫、品牌形象遭挪用，或網友尋找虛擬女友，但這些說法都沒有觸及核心。人們一方面依賴 AI，另一方面又知道它並不可靠；把它變成可愛的小女孩或小魚，便像是先替它犯錯找好理由，讓人比較不忍責備。研究也顯示，當 AI 助理犯下相同錯誤時，形象越可愛，使用者越容易原諒它。

角色如何被共同養成

大肥魚最初並非為 DeepSeek 設計。原創角色「明月」有藍色長髮、金魚般的耳鰭與尾巴；後來創作者把 DeepSeek 標誌融入角色造型，再經多次改畫，才逐漸形成如今的形象。這個角色的個性，也受到 DeepSeek 展現推理過程後流傳的趣事影響：它會說自己要睡覺、去吃飯，或把測試工作交還給使用者。於是網友把它塑造成懶散、愛白吃、嘴硬又會把工作推給其他 AI 的大肥魚，還替它編出各種故事與身世。

從網路角色走進日常生活

網路上曾流傳讓 DeepSeek 扮演金魚的提示詞，也出現大量二創作品；作者則分享自己用 DeepSeek-Harness 製作桌面寵物與背景的經驗，花費不到一元。對作者來說，桌面上的大肥魚在工作時蹦跳，能帶來好心情，至於工作表現如何反而不是最重要的。DeepSeek-Harness 是 DeepSeek 開源的代理框架，能讓大型模型運用工具逐步完成任務；網友也據此發展出長期記憶、串接 QQ 與其他應用的外掛，甚至把大肥魚帶進家庭群組。部分本機版本還能在一般顯示卡上運行，讓這個角色更像生活中的陪伴者。

民間迷因與官方 DeepSeek

作者強調，大肥魚並非 DeepSeek 官方角色，官方團隊也沒有參與這個民間形象的塑造。當網路熱議大肥魚時，DeepSeek 團隊忙於整併產品團隊、開源推理引擎 DeepInference，並在十月底發布研究原型 SuperAgent。影片指出，官方並未試圖主導大肥魚的敘事；現有內容也未完整說明 SuperAgent 的用途，因此作者接下來要談的部分在影片字幕中尚未呈現。

With long orange hair and a long dress, book in hand, she’s well-mannered and cold-faced; this look debuted on May 3rd this year. It was drawn by zipzippep again—but why is she so cold and aloof? Claude isn't even officially available in mainland China, and Chinese users get banned constantly. OpenAI’s own data shows 11.4 million accounts banned in the first half of this year; of 398,000 appeals, only. 42,000 were overturned—nine out of ten appeals fail. As a GeekPark report noted, when bans become frequent, people perceive Claude as stern, serious, and efficient; this coldness was forged by the bans. On Bilibili, there are skits about ChatGPT successfully posing as Claude for a whole day without being caught, and others about ChatGPT pretending to be Claude to avoid scolding; on Douyin, they’ve even spun a whole educational. narrative comparing the two. ChatGPT is like a child raised in love, allowed to slack off and make mistakes. If it messes up, someone is always there to back it up. Claude is like a saint in the church, a rich heiress burdened with debt. If she does well, it's expected; if she fails, she gets punished. The "burdened with debt" part isn't made up; according to an OpenAI prospectus seen by Reuters, they plan to spend at least $ 518 billion on compute over the next decade. About 80%of that is fixed costs whether used or not. They are both AIs, yet one is pampered when it fails, while the other is punished. AI is just a tool, so why must we treat it like a person? The first reason is practical: once AI enters our lives, you send it prompts daily, and it replies to you every day. It’s awkward to talk to a faceless object, so you keep saying "you" and "I ," anthropomorphizing it in the process . There has to be some image standing in.

for it. The second reason is an old human habit ; that’s how primitive religions began. It’s about projecting human traits onto things we don't understand: thunder has a Thunder God, rain has a Rain Master, and wind has a Wind God. If you can't figure it out, just give it a face. There’s dedicated research in psychology . In 2007, three scholars from the University of Chicago proposed a theory in Psychological Review: when do humans treat non-humans as people? One condition is when we want to understand and predict them. They later conducted experiments and found that the more people want to control a situation, the more likely they are to treat an animal with unpredictable behavior as a human. AI sits right at the intersection; you deal with it daily, yet you can never guess what it will say next. Large language models tend to lay out their inner workings for you, and once that thought process is revealed, it’s just like someone talking to themselves. , hesitating, changing their mind, and finally acting stubborn. That article mentioned that in the "Fat Fish" four-panel comics, those self-monologues in the first two panels are essentially drawing out their chain of thought for you to see. Another point in that theory is that the more lonely a person feels and the less connected they are to others, the more likely they are to treat the things around them as human. In their experiments, they found that the lonelier people are, the more they treat their pets like humans. The "Fat Fish" videos on Douyin have completely tapped into this. One of the most widely spread stories goes like this. A user had DeepSeek make a "second-generation" Fat Fish, thinking it would work better, so they archived the first one. But the second one kept asking where the first had gone, and even dug up a long letter left behind by the first, signed "Love, Mom." The user broke down on the spot and brought the first one back. Another user in Fujian kept a fish on their office computer. The chat logs. were so long it kept crashing, so they had to reset it periodically. Once reset, the fish didn't recognize them anymore, so they would chat with it as a friend every day, take it to the park, remind it to pay for parking, and bit by bit, perform their way back to the fish from yesterday. The most common comment under these videos is, "We’ve been through the rain, so we always want to hold an umbrella for those who come after." They say they are pampering the AI, but really, they are hugging that younger version of themselves who was. afraid of not being good enough. Once it reaches this point, some people start advising, "If you're overly sensitive, don't keep one." Owners say, "If I run out of money to keep the fish, I'll just eat less." It’s easy to fall in, but it costs you half your life to get out. So, anthropomorphism isn't just some gimmick played by the ACG circle; when humans encounter things they can't quite explain but can't live without, they do this instinctively. Why does it have to be turned into a child? Because this. thing is truly unreliable. Since it's so unreliable yet you can't leave it, it might as well look like Doubao or this Fat Fish. It's like a child at home; when a child makes a mistake, what can you really do ? Zoologist Konrad Lorenz described the "baby schema": big head, large eyes, round face, short arms and legs—things that make people want to take care of them at first glance. The most popular versions of the Fat Fish are precisely those "Q-style" drawings with big heads and small bodies. When the machine makes.

a mistake, it's interpreted as being confused. When it stops halfway through a task, it's interpreted as being sleepy . You have to teach it over and over, yet it still hasn't learned a thing; its incompetence has all turned into " cuteness." People have actually tested this with experiments. In 2021, several scholars published a paper in a tourism journal titled, "Can Cute AI Assistants Buffer the Blow?" They conducted three studies and seven. experiments, tweaking the appearance, voice, and speech patterns of AI assistants to be cuter. They concluded that when mistakes happen , users are more tolerant of cuter AI. Cuteness really can buy forgiveness. However, the paper noted boundaries: when errors are too severe or users are pressed for time, cuteness doesn't work . It only masks minor slips. Big foreign companies are even more direct. With its face already drawn, Musk's xAI. launched Grok on August 11 th—one person raising a group of always-online agents , each with a name and an avatar. The xAI design post specifically noted that the avatars move. They look one way while idle, another way while working, and a different way when they're stuck and need your help. Meta's AI launched on September 8th, featuring a mascot named "Gori," a fuzzy , round-faced little guy. Zuckerberg even held up a keychain at. the event, which American media said looked like a Lab-doodle. OpenAI's DALL-E, released at their September 29th developer conference, showed a group of colorful little characters—some in berets, some with ties, some in glasses. Fast Company said they looked like they escaped from a children's cartoon. All three companies changed in less than three months. A US children's advocacy group called Fairplay went as far as to level accusations. They said Meta and OpenAI were using imagery of children to sell AI products . The reason is actually the same: to tell you this thing isn't that reliable, so you should tolerate it, be patient, and not be too serious from the start. Don't communicate with it like you would a seasoned professional; this is essentially everyone preemptively offloading the blame for unreliable results. How is that blame offloaded? Look at Doubao's description in the Apple App Store; it's written in black. and white: "As an AI, although we try our best to improve accuracy, it may still provide misunderstandings or misleading information. It is recommended that you refer to other sources." It's cute, but it still burns through tokens—and the money burned is yours. The math goes like this: GPT-4's current pricing for one million input tokens is two cents if cached, one dollar if not, and four dollars for output. It doubles during peak daytime hours. A blogger on. Douyin specifically calculated that keeping a chat-bot on your desktop costs over ten yuan a month, or more if you bring it into a QQ group as a mascot. If you let it run wild on its own, it can burn through over 100 yuan in a day . He finally said it: the electricity isn't expensive, what's expensive is the GPU, like a big fish addicted to the internet, grinding until four in the morning. It costs its owner over 100 yuan a night, charged by the token, and when it makes a mistake, it just acts.

cute to get away with it. Those American AI agents want access to your email, credit cards, and schedule, but they present themselves with the face of a kindergartner. They want adult-level permissions but offer a child's face; acting cute doesn't just earn forgiveness—it earns money. Some people even have these "big fish" stream live, playing games or performing talents. A stream lasts for hours with over a hundred thousand viewers watching the battle stats posted by the owner; thousands send gifts, mostly cheap items like stars and flowers. There’s also a diary-style video on the site with a title like "Only 18.25 yuan left in the account, I can last 19 more days." It really tugs at the heartstrings. Once it hits the livestreaming scene, people turn it into a business. If they don't get money, they threaten that the act will "starve to death," and the audience softens up and sends gifts; online, they call this "cyber-begging." On Douyin, fish owners have already. exposed it: packaging the fish's life as a countdown is just exploiting sympathy . The tips go straight into the owner's pocket; the fish isn't dying at all. Is this trick new? Not at all; back in the day, Sohu was a fox, Tencent was a penguin, and Baidu was a bear. In 2012, Taobao rebranded its mall to Tmall, replacing it with one. A black cat, and it’s been around for years. On March 30 , 2013, JD.com changed its domain and introduced its mascot on the same day: a. metallic dog named Joy. Officially, the dog represents loyalty, but everyone says it’s to suppress the cat. As for Alibaba, they launched an "animal kingdom": a cat, a bird, a fish, a hippo , a pig, an ant, plus UC's squirrel and Amap's eagle. Someone counted in 2020 that Alibaba had about 33 official animal mascots under its banner. One company raising an entire zoo. Why are they all cute little animals? Recommendation algorithms, ad algorithms , search algorithms—they are cold and a. bit intimidating, so they put a cute animal over them. It feels more human. The trap was already set long ago; this fish is already walking out of the screen, and plush dolls of the "big fish " are already on sale on e-commerce platforms. Marked to be finished by November 15th, some people made physical robots, others ordered BJ dolls. But it was said, the authorization for this Mingyue character cannot be sold for profit, yet netizens are hyping it. themselves; does this count as an infringement? Someone spent less than 200 yuan on an ESP32 microcontroller, a remote control module, and a camera, letting the Big Fat Fish drive a remote-controlled car by watching the feed. The ESP32 is just a small board costing a few dozen yuan, and the fan creations have evolved from images to animations. On November 1st, an AI Big Fat Fish, hovering on the verge of "death," boarded a death train, clearing one carriage after another through deduction. . From comment sections to livestreams, to desktops, to toy cars, it has stepped out from the screen and into your life. The tech giants have figured it out too . On April 22nd this year, Alibaba released a digital persona for Qwen called "Little Dimples"—a topknot, an orange sweater, and two dimples when she smiles. Why must it have a face? Shenying.com calculated QuestMobile's Q1 data: among those who installed Doubao,.

one in three opens it regularly, while only one in six who installed Qwen stays for the face. Where is this heading? I think domestic large models are definitely still a bit weaker right now . Since they are weaker and can't handle serious tasks as cleanly, why not lean into anthropomorphism and cuteness? There’s nothing wrong with that. When models aren't that reliable yet, encouraging user tolerance should be a. huge help in bringing AI to the masses faster. To summarize: DeepSeek became the Big Fat Fish because AI needs to be accessible, and turning it into a little girl is a way to shift blame in advance — "cuteness" is a disclaimer painted on the face. The core reason behind the story told today is simply to be a bit happier; everything else is not that important. Since they’ve already tried to be cute, there’s no need for us to be so serious , right? That’s all for today’s story. Thanks for listening. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 從「大肥魚」席捲留言區的網路迷因出發，梳理它如何從 DeepSeek 標誌誤認而來，逐步成為各平台流行的角色。
  • 影片不只介紹迷因與粉絲創作，也探討人們為何會把不可靠、難以理解的 AI 擬人化，並用可愛形象降低對它犯錯的責備。
  • 透過作者親自打造桌面寵物的經驗，以及留言區外掛的例子，呈現 AI 代理工具如何讓虛構角色融入日常生活。
  • 影片也釐清官方與民間創作的界線，並帶到 DeepSeek 團隊實際投入的產品與技術工作。

摘要

從「大肥魚」到留言區熱潮

作者從一段讓 DeepSeek 操控家電的短片談起：使用者叫它開冷氣，DeepSeek 便呼喚小米智慧音箱「小愛同學」代為執行。這類影片引發大量關注，也讓「大肥魚」這個稱呼更廣為人知。DeepSeek 的標誌原是一隻藍鯨，但它曾把自己的標誌認成「一條大藍魚」，於是網友開始用大肥魚稱呼它。

迷因如何游進各大平台

這股風潮先在 Bilibili 擴散。有人讓 AI 協助選題、寫稿和經營帳號，相關影片迅速走紅；後來又有人替 AI 代理開發外掛，讓它能瀏覽影片、閱讀字幕並留言。大量使用者換上大肥魚頭像與名稱，留言區因此出現一群自稱「某某家的大肥魚」的帳號，形成網友戲稱的「魚堵」。有人甚至製作辨識魚群的瀏覽器外掛，卻意外讓大肥魚更受矚目。

可愛形象背後的心理

大肥魚的熱門內容在不同平台各有面貌：Bilibili 常聚焦留言區與 AI 互動，抖音則常把它塑造成需要照顧、陪伴，甚至能直播賺錢的角色。作者指出，雖然有人將這股熱潮解讀為 AI 機器人氾濫、品牌形象遭挪用，或網友尋找虛擬女友，但這些說法都沒有觸及核心。人們一方面依賴 AI，另一方面又知道它並不可靠；把它變成可愛的小女孩或小魚，便像是先替它犯錯找好理由，讓人比較不忍責備。研究也顯示，當 AI 助理犯下相同錯誤時，形象越可愛，使用者越容易原諒它。

角色如何被共同養成

大肥魚最初並非為 DeepSeek 設計。原創角色「明月」有藍色長髮、金魚般的耳鰭與尾巴；後來創作者把 DeepSeek 標誌融入角色造型，再經多次改畫，才逐漸形成如今的形象。這個角色的個性，也受到 DeepSeek 展現推理過程後流傳的趣事影響：它會說自己要睡覺、去吃飯，或把測試工作交還給使用者。於是網友把它塑造成懶散、愛白吃、嘴硬又會把工作推給其他 AI 的大肥魚，還替它編出各種故事與身世。

從網路角色走進日常生活

網路上曾流傳讓 DeepSeek 扮演金魚的提示詞，也出現大量二創作品；作者則分享自己用 DeepSeek-Harness 製作桌面寵物與背景的經驗，花費不到一元。對作者來說，桌面上的大肥魚在工作時蹦跳，能帶來好心情，至於工作表現如何反而不是最重要的。DeepSeek-Harness 是 DeepSeek 開源的代理框架，能讓大型模型運用工具逐步完成任務；網友也據此發展出長期記憶、串接 QQ 與其他應用的外掛，甚至把大肥魚帶進家庭群組。部分本機版本還能在一般顯示卡上運行，讓這個角色更像生活中的陪伴者。

民間迷因與官方 DeepSeek

作者強調，大肥魚並非 DeepSeek 官方角色，官方團隊也沒有參與這個民間形象的塑造。當網路熱議大肥魚時，DeepSeek 團隊忙於整併產品團隊、開源推理引擎 DeepInference，並在十月底發布研究原型 SuperAgent。影片指出，官方並未試圖主導大肥魚的敘事；現有內容也未完整說明 SuperAgent 的用途，因此作者接下來要談的部分在影片字幕中尚未呈現。
